title: Oura Resilience Recovery Gap After Hard Days
dataSources: Oura stress and recovery (`oura:stress`), CPAP therapy sessions (`cpap:session`), oral thermometer readings (`thermometer:reading`), and body-composition scale snapshots (`bodycomp:reading`).
app: Personal health telemetry from Oura, OSCAR CPAP exports, oral thermometer readings, and smart body-composition scales sent to Splunk HEC via APIs and CSV exports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=oura:stress
| sort 0 _time
| eval hard_day=if(stress_score>=80,1,0), recovered=if(recovery_score>=70,1,0)
| streamstats current=f last(eval(if(hard_day=1,_time,null()))) as last_hard_day
| where recovered=1 AND isnotnull(last_hard_day)
| eval recovery_days=round((_time-last_hard_day)/86400,1)
| stats avg(recovery_days) as avg_recovery_days perc90(recovery_days) as p90_recovery_days
description: Examines recovery gap after high-stress days. Runs scheduled SPL against `index=personal` to surface **Oura Resilience Recovery Gap After Hard Days** so you can spot drift before it becomes a habit.
value: Recovery lag says more about resilience than a single stressful day ever will.
implementation: Send recovery gap after high-stress days events to `index=personal` with the fields used in this SPL and review the outliers or trend breaks regularly.
visualization: Table or chart of recovery gap after high-stress days, depending on the selected time range.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Oura Ring — Oura Cloud API v2 → HEC scripted input.
• **Subcategory context**: Advanced Health & Biohacking — typical feeds: HRV (`hrv:reading`), blood oxygen (`spo2:reading`), lab panels (`bloodpanel:result`), supplements (`supplement:intake`), continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), sleep-apnea events (`apnea:event`), body co.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `oura:stress`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Oura Ring** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=oura:stress`.

**Collection method:** Oura Cloud API v2 → HEC scripted input.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `GET /v2/usercollection/daily_sleep`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 86400s (daily sync).

**Key fields to extract:** `score, contributors, heart_rate, hrv`.

**Typical connector stack:** Biohacking data — HRV straps, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure cuffs, continuous glucose monitors, body-composition scales, lab-result exports, and supplement logs — ingested to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Send recovery gap after high-stress days events to `index=personal` with the fields used in this SPL and review the outliers or trend breaks regularly.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "oura:stress", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:stress earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Oura Resilience Recovery Gap After Hard Days** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=oura:stress`) across the full search range. `eventstats` / `streamstats` compute rolling baselines before filtering outliers; window size controls sensitivity (smaller window = noisier alerts).

**Fields this search depends on:** `hard_day`, `recovery_score`, `stress_score`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:stress
| sort 0 _time
| eval hard_day=if(stress_score>=80,1,0), recovered=if(recovery_score>=70,1,0)
| streamstats current=f last(eval(if(hard_day=1,_time,null()))) as last_hard_day
| where recovered=1 AND isnotnull(last_hard_day)
| eval recovery_days=round((_time-last_hard_day)/86400,1)
| stats avg(recovery_days) as avg_recovery_days perc90(recovery_days) as p90_recovery_days
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Oura app → Readiness / Sleep tabs. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:stress earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table hard_day, recovery_score, stress_score
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:stress earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `stress_score` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:stress earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(stress_score) AS p50 perc90(stress_score) AS p90 perc99(stress_score) AS p99 max(stress_score) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.25.20: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Or Chart Of Recovery Gap After High-Stress Days (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.

**Panel 2 — Depending On The Selected Time Range (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Oura Ring — no Oura Ring events / missing fields:** If `oura:stress` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Oura Ring connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Oura Ring — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Oura Ring JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=oura:stress | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Oura Ring — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Oura Ring — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Oura Ring APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Everything is an outlier:** Baseline window is too short or `stdev=0` — require minimum sample count (`where count>=5`) before computing z-scores.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
grandmaExplanation: It records what is happening with recovery gap after high-stress days, so odd changes stand out quickly.
